t: In front of you in Berkeley Square is Nymph, a statue by the sculptor Alexander Munro. Munro belonged to the Pre-Raphaelite movement and worked mainly in portraits and statues. He's best known for his group Paolo and Francesca, from 1852, often seen as the epitome of Pre-Raphaelite sculpture. The statue also commemorates Henry Petty-Fitzmaurice, the third Marquess of Lansdowne, a statesman who served in every Whig or Liberal ministry from 1806 to 1863, and who was Home Secretary and Chancellor of the Exchequer.
